items.summary: Interpretability is considered by many a major bottleneck for alignment. As a result, a lot of people who are concerned about AI safety, and especially about extinction risk and other catastrophic risks, work on interpretability. In this post, I want to argue that better interpretability methods would likely speed up capabilities dramatically. Worse, they would speed up capabilities much more than they would speed up alignment. This is true for the current world, and for any world without extremely high levels of coordination and sanity about ASI development. Under any worldview where faster capabilities progress makes catastrophe more likely, we should expect progress in interpretability to make the odds of catastrophe much worse. To put it briefly, this is because the better we get at interpretability, the more AI will be able to read…
items.title: Advances in interpretability would boost capabilities more than alignment

items.summary: AI may radically change our conception of “who is in an org”. Historically, there is a sharp delineation between an org’s staff (on the “inside”), versus its users (on the “outside”). The relationship of a fulltime employee of an org is radically different than that of one of its customers. This is especially true for consumer tech startups & companies: think Google, Meta, Reddit, X, now perhaps OpenAI and Anthropic. With AI however, the bar for an external user to be able to contribute, drops drastically. At the same time, employing and compensating this user will be much easier, as AI obliterates transaction costs. Overall, I expect org boundaries to become much more porous: more part-time workers, more volunteers, more collectives and communes. items.summary: Or: The payload lens on Darwin Tl;dr: What is the most natural teleological shorthand to use, when thinking about evolution? The “gene-centered view” of e.g. Dawkins says: genes are “trying” to increase the number of exact copies of themselves. And organisms are “vehicles” genes use to survive. The “payload lens” (which I’ll be pitching) says: adaptive payloads (such as eyesight or fair meiosis) are “trying” to become deeper, stabler attractor basins that can team up with other adaptive payloads. And genes are “vehicles” these payloads use to survive. Epistemic status: I haven’t done much of a lit search, so I’m claiming neither that any of this is original nor that it is vetted/established; I’m laying it out partly because I want to be able to build on it in some later essays about what we humans are (and what some possible AIs might…

items.summary: Currently, the public has very little insight about the robustness of alignment methods used by AGI companies. It’s possible that, when an AGI company notices some misaligned behavior (e.g. through an alignment evaluation, or through noticing real-world misbehavior), they conduct a principled investigation and address root causes of the misalignment. It’s also possible that they directly try to train away the examples of misalignment, which could result in brittle alignment that does not generalize out-of-distribution. Without additional information from within AI companies about how they align their models (especially in response to egregious cases of misalignment, e.g. cybersecurity incidents), the public cannot adequately reason about risks from misalignment. items.summary: We study the perfect loop space $LX$ of a proper scheme $X$ over a local field $F$. We show that if $X$ contains a rational curve, then $LX$ is not ind-representable, even in a very weak sense. We also show that if $X$ admits a proper model $\mathfrak{X}$ over the integers $\mathcal{O}$ of $F$, whose geometric special fiber does not contain rational curves, then $L^+\mathfrak{X} \stackrel{\sim}{\to} LX$ is an isomorphism via the natural map, where $L^+\mathfrak{X}$ denotes the perfect positive loop space (jet scheme) of $\mathfrak{X}$. In particular, $LX$ is a scheme in this case.

items.summary: AI safety evaluations often involve sensitive prompts and proprietary models. Evaluators want to keep their evaluation prompts secret from model owners to prevent purposeful or incidental data leakage, ensuring longer usefulness of their benchmark. Model owners in turn wish to keep their proprietary model weights and inference code within their own secure infrastructure to protect their IP. We present a way forward for "double-blind evals", which provide cryptographic guarantees that an evaluator's prompts are not shared with the model owner, while simultaneously maintaining the confidentiality of the model weights and inference code. To accomplish this, we use secure enclaves that encrypt data in RAM at the hardware level. To this end, we encode intra-modal geometry for each modality and reduce cross-modal structural discrepancies through a dynamically learned GW barycenter, thereby encouraging structural consistency in addition to instance-level contrastive alignment. items.summary: As a fundamental cryptographic primitive, secret sharing distributes a secret among multiple parties and allows certain authorized parties to recover the secret while preventing unauthorized parties from knowing the secret. However, local leakage from each party member allows an adversary to learn partial information from each share, which is not guaranteed by traditional security. In this paper, we study bounds on the reconstruction threshold of Shamir's secret sharing scheme over prime fields against arbitrary 1-bit local leakage. We show that, for all sufficiently large $n$ and every prime $p>n$, the $(n,t)$-Shamir's scheme is $\exp(-Ω(n))$-resilient whenever $t/n\geq 0.489$, for any choice of distinct nonzero evaluation points. Our proof refines the dual-code list recovery analysis and combines complementary Fourier estimates…

items.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) from raw sensory inputs such as images or onboard sensors can be challenging due to high-dimensional observations and sparse rewards. A common strategy is to train a teacher policy with access to privileged state information and then distill it into a student policy that acts from raw inputs alone. However, when the teacher relies on information unavailable to the student, exact imitation may be impossible, creating an irreducible imitation gap. Existing approaches typically mitigate this mismatch through careful reward shaping or additional reinforcement learning on the student policy after the teacher has been trained. items.summary: Transformers are built with continuous symmetries in the attention mechanism. We derive $ρ$, a scalar invariant that measures each head's capacity to couple to rotary positional encodings. This framework allows us to analyze heads without forward passes, opening a new research direction into data-independent analysis of modern LLMs. Empirically, we find that $ρ$ predicts induction heads, the most-studied circuit type in mechanistic interpretability, with Spearman correlation between $-0.55$ and $-0.74$ across four bias-free RoPE models spanning $135$M to $7$B parameters. As a preliminary proof of concept, we use $ρ$ to apply YaRN to only the top-50% positional heads, which degrades perplexity less than uniform application. Code is available at https://github.com/MPedraBento/rho-invariant.
items.title: A Geometric Invariant of Attention Predicts Head Specialization from Weights Alone

The method is developed within a cell-centered formulation on moving quadrilateral meshes, where discrete divergence and curl operators are constructed from vertex-based differential operators. Natural-language requirements leave ample room for specification gaming, producing systems that blaze through benchmarks while silently losing updates or violating consistency. Worse, each research iteration consumes tokens, while validating a candidate under real concurrency, memory pressure, and failure conditions can stretch the entire research process into weeks. It then wanted the planet to have a uniform gentle server hum, with no deviation. People were forced to wear breathing masks which cut the sound off at the source. This level of autism was unthinkable. Houses had sound strippers and sound-proof transperant windows. The quietness is actively oppressive. I constantly due to my social nature feel like I am going to asphyxiate to death. But the ASI will not budge on this. — News Report in Human Proceedings, circa. 2080 (link to full post: https://clasz.substack.com/p/subpar-results)

Scott Alexander's 2018 essay The Omnigenic Model As Metaphor for Life is a clear statement of what has become general rationalist doctrine on multicausality. items.summary: We consider a kinetic model for bacterial chemotaxis that describes the propagation of traveling pulses driven by a nutrient and a self-produced chemoattractant. items.summary: AI agents are increasingly capable of discovering new mathematical results, yet their reasoning and generated proofs can be difficult to understand and verify. We introduce an interpretable framework for AI-guided mathematical discovery, focused on improving quantitative bounds on analytic constants. items.summary: Cyber-physical smart-grid detectors are typically treated as black boxes and validated exclusively on clean, temporally shuffled datasets, which risk overly optimistic performance claims. items.summary: The field of mechanistic interpretability is well-suited to collaborative projects between mathematicians and AI researchers. This work describes one such project. We trained a small transformer to learn the language of the Coxeter group affine A2, best known as the symmetries of the tiling of the Euclidean plane by equilateral triangles. We then formulated and proved a word-theoretic conjecture about affine A2 after observing the attention patterns of the trained model.

items.summary: Reinforcement learning for large language model post-training often reuses each batch of sampled rollouts for several gradient passes to amortize the cost of generation. In this paper, we propose Permute-then-Adapt (PTA), a framework that leverages efficient weak models to identify missed positives while controlling Type-I error relative to a conditional permutation reference, up to calibration approximation error. items.summary: Today's LLM-based agents are vulnerable to deception by users and other agents. Defending against deception requires Theory of Mind (ToM) reasoning to infer the beliefs and goals of others as well as modeling tactics based on communication theory. items.summary: We study homeopathic learning, a phenomenon where poisoned training data with little effect on its own can create a hidden backdoor once clean, contrasting data is added. items.summary: We study the problem of synchronizing two players in a \emph{distributed multi-armed bandit} setting. The probability of \emph{synchronization error} is analyzed by recasting synchronization as a \emph{communication problem}. Using a well-designed random coding ensemble, we derive error exponents for the maximum-likelihood decoder. We then introduce a \emph{universal decoder} that achieves the same error exponents as the optimal decoder. items.summary: Cross-Layer Transcoders (CLTs) decompose the activations of large language models into human-interpretable features and trace how these features interact across layers to form circuits, making them a key tool for mechanistic interpretability. Beyond the usual trade-off between sparsity and reconstruction quality, a CLT has to model all layers at once, which adds a further challenge. The common JumpReLU recipe controls sparsity only indirectly through a penalty, while the direct extension of TopK selects a fixed number of latents in every layer.
